messages.text: uhh... i don't even know where to start rn. kinda freaking out a little just opening this chat tbh.

It is completely okay to feel shaky when starting a conversation like this. You don't need to find the perfect words or have a clear plan right now. I am here to support you at whatever pace feels manageable for you. Would you like to take a deep breath together before we continue?

yeah... i tried to stop, i really did. but it's like... when the pressure builds up, i don't know how else to let it out. and now mom knows, therapy’s happening, everyone’s watching — and i still can’t get it together. feels so stupid.

It makes complete sense that you feel overwhelmed when so many people are involved in your journey. Please know that struggling does not make you stupid; it simply shows how hard this process actually is. The pressure to "get it together" immediately can make the weight feel even heavier than it needs to be. I am here to listen without judgment, so you don't have to carry that alone.

i just keep thinking... why can't i be normal? like, other people go through hell and don't turn into a mess. i should be stronger. it's just skin, right? but i can't stop. and now i'm dragging my mom into it, my therapist, and now you... i'm so tired of being a burden.

You are not a burden for needing support, and healing is rarely a straight line. Everyone copes with pressure differently, and your struggle does not make you weaker than others. The people around you are involved because they want to help, not because they think you are failing. Facing this pain takes immense strength, even when it feels like you are losing control.

it just feels like... every time someone tries to help, i mess it up. like i’m proving them right — that i’m too broken to fix. and the worst part? i don’t even care sometimes. or i do, but not enough to stop. does that make me a lost cause?

That feeling of being a lost cause is often the pain talking, not the truth about who you are. It is very common to feel torn between wanting to stop and feeling unable to do so. Your worth is not defined by your ability to fix yourself perfectly or quickly. I am here to walk this path with you, exactly where you are right now.
it’s not just the cutting... it’s the lying. hiding. feeling like i’m letting everyone down. i hate that i can’t just *stop* and make it all go away. like... why is this so hard for me?

That secrecy often comes from a place of shame, not because you are fundamentally broken or unlovable. It is incredibly hard to stop behaviors that once helped you survive overwhelming emotions. You are not letting anyone down by struggling; you are navigating something very difficult. I am here to support you without judgment, regardless of the pace of your healing.
it just keeps going in circles... i cut, i feel guilty, i promise i’ll stop, then i do it again. i can’t even look at myself sometimes. feels like i’m stuck in this... loop i can’t get out of.

It is understandable that you feel trapped when the cycle of guilt and action repeats so quickly. Your worth is not defined by your ability to break this pattern immediately. Beating yourself up often makes the loop feel tighter, but you don't have to face that shame alone. I am here to support you through the guilt and the struggle, not just the stopping.
i keep trying to white-knuckle it, but that doesn’t work. is there... like, something i can actually *do* when it hits? instead of just trying not to?

You are absolutely right that willpower alone is rarely enough to stop intense urges. There are grounding techniques, like holding ice or focusing on intense sensory details, that can help you ride out the wave safely. The goal is to find a substitute that gives you relief without causing harm. Would you like to try identifying one small tool to use the next time the urge hits?
yeah... i guess i could try something. like what? ice? that’d be weird but... i dunno, maybe. i’ll try it. *if* i remember. and *if* i don’t just ignore it.

Doubting whether it will work is a very common part of trying to change old patterns. It is okay if you ignore it sometimes; the goal is just to have the option there. You could try writing that word "ice" somewhere visible so it pops into your head later. I am here to support you through the attempts, regardless of the outcome.
could we... like, come up with a few options? in case ice feels stupid in the moment? maybe something else that’s weird but works?

It is really smart to have a backup plan in case one method doesn't feel right in the moment. You might try biting into a lemon or holding a heavy object to ground your body physically. Some people find shaking out their arms or splashing cold water on their face helps break the tension too. Let’s pick the one that feels least strange to you, and we can make it part of your plan.

huh. i never thought about having a whole... list. like a plan. i always just waited till it hit and then tried to fight it. maybe having options will help. even if i fail, at least i tried something different?

That is a really powerful insight, and having a plan can make those moments feel less overwhelming. Trying something different is definitely a success, even if the urge doesn't go away completely. You are learning to navigate this differently, and that is progress in itself. We can add to that list together right now if you feel up to it.
can we just... stick to what to do when it happens? i’m not ready to go back into why it started. just wanna focus on stopping the cycle now.

Absolutely, we can focus entirely on practical tools for right now. You do not need to explore the past to find ways to stay safe today. Building a list of coping options is a powerful step toward breaking the cycle. I am here to help you fill that list out whenever you feel up to it.
yeah. thanks. i... i actually feel a tiny bit lighter? like, not fixed or anything. but less alone. i’ll try the ice thing. and the cold water. maybe write it on my hand so i don’t ignore it.

It is wonderful to hear that you are feeling a tiny bit lighter and less alone right now. You are absolutely right that healing doesn't mean being instantly fixed or perfect. Writing those options on your hand is a practical way to keep them close when the urge comes. I am here to support you whenever you need to reach out again.
thanks for not making me feel like a lost cause. it helps... more than i can say.

I am so glad to hear that you are feeling a little less alone in this. You are definitely not a lost cause, and your feelings matter deeply. Healing takes time, but you are taking brave steps today. I will always be here to listen without judgment.
